references.text: Jesus says that whoever does not hate father and mother, wife, children, brothers and sisters, yes, even their own life, cannot be his disciple. This expresses the same radical demand to prioritize God's kingdom over family relationships as in [ref:Luk 14:26|Luke 14:26].

The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus gives the same promise to those who have left houses, brothers, sisters, father, mother, children or fields for his name's sake ([ref:Matt 19:29|Matthew 19:29]).

The parallel passage in Mark where Jesus promises a hundredfold return to anyone who has left houses, brothers, sisters, mother, father, children or fields for his and the gospel's sake ([ref:Mark 10:29-30|Mark 10:29-30]).

The tribe of Levi, which said about their father and mother: "I do not see him", and who did not know their brothers or children, but kept the Lord's word. An Old Testament example of placing God's call above family ties ([ref:5 Mos 33:9|Deuteronomy 33:9]).
The immediate continuation where Jesus promises that whoever has left these things will receive many times more in this time and eternal life in the coming world ([ref:Luk 18:30|Luke 18:30]).
Jesus calls people to follow him without turning back to say goodbye to their family or bury their father – the same radical demand to prioritize God's kingdom ([ref:Luk 9:59-62|Luke 9:59-62]).

Paul counts everything as loss compared to knowing Christ Jesus, his Lord, and has given up all for Christ's sake – a personal fulfillment of Jesus' words about leaving everything for the sake of God's kingdom ([ref:Fil 3:8|Philippians 3:8]).

Moses gave up being called the son of Pharaoh's daughter and chose rather to suffer with God's people, considering Christ's disgrace greater wealth than Egypt's treasures – an example of leaving everything for the sake of God's kingdom ([ref:Hebr 11:24-26|Hebrews 11:24-26]).
